data.name: Arbaagtan
data.gender_notes: Arbaagtan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Arbaa' meaning forty and the Persian suffix 'tan' meaning ten, 'Arbaagtan' translates to 'forty ten'. This name is given to babies born on the fortieth day after their birth, or to signify the forty virtues of Islam. The name Arbaagtan carries the meaning “Forty” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Arbaagtan usually hope their child will grow to embody forty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with spiritual significance, 'Arbaagtan' represents the journey towards spiritual growth and the acquisition of forty virtues.
data.etymology: Arbaagtan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Forty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arbaagtan total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: أرباعتن
in_arabic.long_meaning: أَرْبَاعَتن، اسم علم مسلم، مشتق من الجذر الرابع في العربية، ويعني الحماسة والشجاعة والاستقامة، ويستخدم في القرآن الكريم للإشارة إلى المخلصين والصادقين، وكان phổباً عند المسلمين في العصور الوسطى، ويُعد اسمًا من الأسماء الكريمة في الإسلام، ويصف الشخص الذي يمتلك الحماس والشجاعة في خدمة الدين، ويُعتبر من الأسماء التي تُشجع على الصدق واليقين، ويُستخدم في جميع أنحاء العالم الإسلامي.

in_english.name: Arbaagtan
in_english.meaning: Arbaagtan means a strong and courageous person who follows Islam
in_english.long_meaning: Arbaagtan is an Arabic name that originates from the fourth root of the Arabic language. It means strong and courageous. The name is mentioned several times in the Quran and is associated with the qualities of a righteous person. In Islamic tradition, the name Arbaagtan is given to children born to parents who are known for their strength and courage in following the path of Islam. The name is also associated with the qualities of loyalty, honesty, and determination. In modern times, the name Arbaagtan has become popular in many Muslim countries and is considered a symbol of strength and courage.

data.cultural_impact: The naming tradition 'Arbaagtan' has historical significance rooted in Islamic culture. The practice dates back to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) who set the precedent by giving the name Arba'ah (Arabic for forty) to his grandson, Imam Hasan al-Askari (as).This event was recorded in Hadith (traditions of the Prophet's sayings and actions) and became a practice in some Muslim communities, particularly the Shia sect. The custom is a reminder of the importance of celebrating new life and family connections within the context of Islamic traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the number forty holds deep symbolism. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is said to have fasted for forty nights consecutively during one of his retreats to Mount Hira' (the Night Journey or Isra' and Mi'raj). Forty is also the number of prescription sets in Islamic medical Jurisprudence (Fiqh), and the justice scale in the Islamic Adl (equity/justice) symbol contains forty lines. By giving the name 'Arbaagtan', a newborn is imbued with spiritual significance from an early age. Parents hope that their child will embody the virtues and ideals of Islam, represented by this auspicious number.
